title: Bridge Truss Stress Analysis Viewer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive bridge truss stress analysis viewer with the following specifications:

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 25) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from (10,15,10) white intensity 0.8, one from (-8,10,-5) blue-tinted (0x8888ff) intensity 0.3.
- A ground plane at y=-0.5 (gray, 0x333344, 60x60) with grid helper.
- OrbitControls enabled for camera manipulation.

## Bridge Truss Structure
- Build a Warren truss bridge with exactly 11 bottom chord nodes spaced 3 units apart along X axis (from x=-15 to x=15), at y=0.
- 10 top chord nodes at y=5, offset by 1.5 units in X from bottom nodes (triangulated pattern), from x=-13.5 to x=13.5.
- Connect nodes with cylindrical members (radius 0.08): bottom chord (10 members), top chord (9 members), and diagonal/vertical web members forming the Warren pattern (20 web members). Total ~39 members.
- Each member is a THREE.Mesh with CylinderGeometry. Store member data in an array: {id, nodeA, nodeB, mesh, restLength, stress, force}.
- Nodes at index 0 (left) and 10 (right) of the bottom chord are fixed supports (pinned). Render small triangular support indicators beneath them.

## Material System
- Members change color based on stress: blue (0x0066ff) for compression, red (0xff3300) for tension, green (0x00cc44) for near-zero stress (abs < 0.05).
- Stress intensity maps to color saturation/brightness. Use a continuous color gradient.
- Member thickness visually scales slightly with abs(stress): radius from 0.06 (low) to 0.14 (high stress).

## Load System
- Support point loads applied to any bottom chord node (except the two fixed supports, indices 0 and 10).
- The currently selected node is highlighted with a yellow (0xffff00) sphere (radius 0.3).
- Default: no loads applied. User adds/removes loads interactively.
- Each load is visualized as a downward red arrow (ArrowHelper) at the node, scaled proportionally to load magnitude.
- Maximum load per node: 100 kN. Load step: 10 kN.

## Stress Analysis (Simplified Method of Joints)
- Implement a simplified static analysis: when loads change, solve for member forces using a direct stiffness or method-of-joints approximation.
- For simplification, use the following approach: each loaded node distributes force to connected members proportionally to their geometric alignment with the vertical load direction. Members closer to supports accumulate more force.
- Compute reaction forces at the two supports. Sum of reactions must equal sum of applied loads (equilibrium). Left reaction = sum(P_i * (L - x_i)) / L, Right reaction = sum(P_i * x_i) / L where L=30 (bridge length).
- After solving, normalize stress values to range [-1, 1] where -1 is max compression and +1 is max tension.
- Verify: sum of all vertical force components (reactions - loads) === 0 (within epsilon 0.001).

## User Interactions
- Click on bottom chord nodes (raycasting) to select them. Selected node gets yellow highlight.
- Arrow Up / Arrow Down: increase/decrease load on selected node by 10 kN (clamp 0-100).
- Key 'R': reset all loads to zero, clear all arrows, reset all member colors to green.
- Key 'D': toggle deformation visualization mode. When active, nodes displace proportionally to computed forces (exaggerated 50x for visibility). Members stretch/compress visually.
- Key 'M': cycle through display modes: 'stress' (color by stress), 'force' (color by absolute force magnitude, yellow gradient), 'neutral' (all members white).
- Key 'U': undo last load change (maintain history stack of up to 20 states).
- Key 'E': redo last undone load change.
- Key 'S': toggle display of stress value labels (CSS2DRenderer or sprite labels) on each member showing numeric stress value.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left panel (semi-transparent dark background, white text):
  - Title: 'Bridge Truss Stress Analysis'
  - Selected node index and its current load
  - Total applied load (sum of all node loads)
  - Left support reaction and right support reaction
  - Display mode indicator
  - Deformation mode on/off
  - Equilibrium check: show 'BALANCED' in green if abs(sum_reactions - sum_loads) < 0.001, else 'UNBALANCED' in red
- Bottom bar with buttons: [Reset Loads] [Toggle Deformation] [Cycle Mode] [Undo] [Redo] [Toggle Labels]

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- nodeCount: number (should be 21 total: 11 bottom + 10 top)
- memberCount: number (should be ~39)
- selectedNode: number or null (index of selected bottom chord node)
- loads: array of numbers, length 11, load on each bottom chord node (kN)
- totalLoad: number (sum of loads)
- reactionLeft: number (left support reaction force)
- reactionRight: number (right support reaction force)
- equilibriumError: number (abs(reactionLeft + reactionRight - totalLoad))
- isBalanced: boolean (equilibriumError < 0.001)
- displayMode: string ('stress' | 'force' | 'neutral')
- deformationActive: boolean
- labelsVisible: boolean
- memberStresses: array of numbers (normalized stress for each member)
- maxStress: number (max absolute stress value across all members)
- minStress: number (min stress value, most compressive)
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- historyLength: number (total actions performed)
- supportReactionsSum: number (reactionLeft + reactionRight)
- loadedNodeCount: number (count of nodes with load > 0)
physics_constraints: Static equilibrium: sum of vertical reactions must equal sum of applied loads (reactionLeft + reactionRight === totalLoad within epsilon 0.001). Reaction forces computed as: reactionLeft = sum(P_i * (L - x_i)) / L, reactionRight = sum(P_i * x_i) / L where L = 30. Member stresses must be NaN-free and bounded in [-1, 1]. Loads clamped to [0, 100] per node. Deformation displacements proportional to forces, exaggerated for visualization only. Conservation: total load energy is distributed across members without loss.
